page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring direct hardware access. Built on the Intel x86_64 architecture operating at up to 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated hardware threads. With 1536.0 GB of total system RAM, it maintains an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, designed to process large memory-resident datasets without virtualization overhead.

Storage and interconnect resources are provisioned directly to the bare-metal chassis, featuring 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 300 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include discrete graphics processing units, directing all electrical and thermal budgets toward x86 CPU throughput, volatile memory capacity, and local and network I/O pathways. The configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing for external connectivity.

Eliminating hypervisor abstraction provides predictable, low-latency execution across all cores and memory channels. This resource density aligns with workloads that demand sustained CPU performance, high network bandwidth, and dense local flash storage, such as enterprise in-memory databases, large distributed caching systems, and high-throughput transactional data platforms.
